title: Senior Video Editor
location: Remote — North, Central or South America
summary: Own our short-form edits, thumbnails and motion templates for premium brands in home building, design and lifestyle.
intro: Peak Exposure Media is a video-first content agency in Utah. We make cinematic, polished social content for premium brands in home building, design and lifestyle, and we're hiring a full-time senior editor to own our short-form edits, thumbnails and motion templates.
We hire for four things: creative bravery, excellence over easy, client obsession and an ownership mentality. If that sounds like how you already work, you'll like it here.
processNote: Our process has three steps, all before an interview. We reply to everyone within 24 hours of each step.

values.name: Excellence Over Easy
values.desc: Quality matters; don't rush or choose the easy route.

values.name: Client-Obsessed
values.desc: Care deeply about the client's results, not just completing deliverables.

values.name: Ownership Mentality
values.desc: Act like it's your company, not just a job.

assessment.title: Written Assessment
assessment.blurb: About 25 minutes. Six questions about how you think. Each answer is capped at 150 words.

questions.prompt: Watch this PEM video and tell us: what works, what would you change, and why?
questions.strong: Specific, confident critique of a real choice (the hook, a cut, the music). Not flattery, not "it's great."

questions.prompt: You get 3 hours of raw footage and a brief for a 20-minute YouTube video. Walk us through your first two hours of work.
questions.strong: A system: ingest, organize, selects or stringout, structure before cutting. Juniors start cutting immediately.

questions.prompt: A client says the edit "doesn't feel right" but can't say why. What do you do, step by step?
questions.strong: Asks diagnostic questions, offers two options, owns the fix. Doesn't blame the client or the brief.

questions.prompt: Tell us about a time a round of revisions frustrated you. What happened and what did you do?
questions.strong: Honest about the frustration, then describes what they changed in their own process. Red flag: the story is about how the client was wrong.

questions.prompt: Describe a time you pushed an edit somewhere safer would have been easier, and it paid off. What was the risk?
questions.strong: A real creative risk with a real reason. Red flag: can't think of one, or the "risk" was a trendy transition.

questions.prompt: Look at our Instagram and one of our client accounts. In three sentences, describe our editing style and one thing you'd bring to it.
questions.strong: Names concrete traits (cinematic, clean type, restrained pacing) and a contribution that fits rather than fights the style.

test.title: Test Edit
test.blurb: A real brief, real footage, 4–6 hours of work over 72 hours. Unpaid, tightly scoped, and the single most important part of the process.
packageNotes: Raw footage: showroom b-roll and talking-head takes of Brandon Jensen
That's it on purpose. No reference edit, no music, no templates — we want to see what you come up with, not a copy of ours

brief.p: Paragon Custom Construction — a high-end builder in Utah. This footage is from their build-out of a showroom for Schumacher, a luxury fabric and wallcovering house. Two premium brands are on screen at once: the builder and the design firm.
Affluent homeowners, architects and interior designers who hire builders at this level. They are visually literate and bored by generic content.
One Instagram Reel, vertical 9:16, 1080×1920, 30–60 seconds, H.264.

Elegant and high-end with a hint of social trend. Think a luxury brand that understands Instagram, not a TikTok editor doing luxury. Restrained pacing, clean motion, no stock SFX, no meme fonts, no trendy transitions for their own sake. It still has to work as social content: a hook in the first two seconds and something that re-earns attention every few seconds.

brief.h: Brandon's talking video must be in the cut
brief.p: Pick the single best take or mix takes together — your call. Cut him for clarity and pace; do not use every word.
Color correct and polish the footage so it looks premium and consistent across shots. The footage is not log. LUTs are fine; we're looking at your eye for skin tones, matching and overall finish.

Burned-in, every spoken word, set in Degular. It's available in Premiere Pro through Adobe Fonts (Graphics panel → font menu → search “Degular” and activate); if you don't see it, it's free to activate at fonts.adobe.com with your Creative Cloud login. Typography should look designed, not defaulted.
Source your own track. Royalty-free or licensed, your choice — the selection is part of the test.
One strong cover image for the Reel as a PNG, 1080×1920. It should work as a still on the grid and be on-brand for both Paragon and Schumacher.

The Premiere Pro project file (zipped, with media relinked to the folder structure you received), and your start and finish times — track them from the moment you open the footage to the final export.

If you'd like, record a 2–3 minute Loom walking through your choices: the hook, the take selection, the color, anything you'd do differently with more time. It's optional, but it's the fastest way for us to understand how you think. Loom is free at loom.com — install the Chrome extension or desktop app, hit record with your screen and mic on, play through your edit while you talk, stop, and paste the share link below.
72 hours from when you unlock this page. Questions about the brief are welcome — there's a field for them below.

anchors.1: First 2 seconds are slow or generic; no pattern breaks
anchors.3: Clear hook; pacing holds through the middle
anchors.5: Hook lands instantly; every 5–7 seconds something re-earns attention

anchors.1: Cuts feel random or metronomic; no breathing room
anchors.3: Cuts follow the music and the story
anchors.5: Edit has a felt rhythm; pauses are deliberate; it breathes

anchors.1: Audio uneven, color inconsistent, type sloppy
anchors.3: Clean mix, matched color, readable type
anchors.5: Broadcast-level mix, graded, typography that looks designed

anchors.1: Uncorrected or mismatched shots; skin tones off; a LUT dropped on with no adjustment
anchors.3: Clean correction, matched shots, natural skin tones
anchors.5: A deliberate, consistent look that suits both brands; could pass for a colorist's work

anchors.1: Default presets, off-brand fonts, cover is a screengrab
anchors.3: Clean on-brand type; cover frame is composed
anchors.5: Custom templated motion; cover frame could run as an ad

anchors.1: Ignored length, tone or deliverable spec
anchors.5: Hit every spec and made one smart call the brief didn't ask for

anchors.1: Project file is a mess; hours implausible
anchors.3: Labeled bins, tidy timeline; hours in the 4–6 range
anchors.5: Project file others could work from; efficient hours, better result

anchors.1: Only one lane in the portfolio
anchors.3: Credible short-form plus one other format
anchors.5: Senior-level across short-form, long-form and product

bravery.1: Edit is competent but forgettable; critique is polite; can't name a creative risk
bravery.3: Makes one distinct choice and can defend it
bravery.5: The edit has a point of view; critique is sharp and specific; a real risk with a real reason

excellence.1: Shortcuts visible: presets, unmixed audio, messy project, missed naming spec
excellence.3: Clean work, specs met, hours plausible
excellence.5: Every detail handled; project file reusable; chose the harder-but-better option and said so

client.1: Talks only about the edit; client is an obstacle; describes style but not the client
client.3: Mentions the client's goal; handles pushback with questions, not defensiveness
client.5: Frames every choice by what it does for the client's audience; would calm an actual client

ownership.1: Blames client, brief or footage; no questions asked; late without notice
ownership.3: Owns the fix; hits the deadline; asks at least one clarifying question
ownership.5: Treats the brief like their own project; flags a problem and solves it; explains trade-offs like a partner

decision.advanceToCall: Skill ≥ 3.5 with no criterion at 1, brief adherence ≥ 3, every value ≥ 3
decision.hireBar: Skill ≥ 4 and Values ≥ 4 after the call
